lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Paul's letter to the Romans, from the greeting and the gospel theme (1:1-17) to its closing greetings and doxology (16:27).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Romans is about, using 1:16-17?
ev: State the letter's theme from 1:16-17
Describe the movement: sin (1-3), justification (3-5), life in Christ and the Spirit (6-8), Israel (9-11), Christian living (12-16)

nodes.t: The gospel is the power of God
nodes.d: Paul introduces himself and states the letter's theme: the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, and in it the righteousness of God is revealed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 1:16-17?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 1:16-17
Say what Paul calls himself in 1:1

nodes.d: Paul says God's wrath is revealed against ungodliness and that people suppress the truth about God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about knowing God from creation in Romans 1?
ev: State what Paul says can be known of God from creation (1:19-20)

nodes.d: God will judge each person according to his works with no partiality; Jew and Gentile alike.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Romans 2 teaches about God's judgment?
ev: Explain "there is no respect of persons with God" (2:11)

nodes.d: Paul gathers Old Testament testimony to show that all are under sin and that no one is justified by the works of the law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says every mouth is stopped (3:19)?
ev: State the conclusion of 3:19-20
Quote or paraphrase 3:23

nodes.d: The righteousness of God is through faith in Jesus Christ for all who believe; we are justified freely by his grace through the redemption in Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 3:21-26 says a sinner is justified?
ev: Explain "justified freely by his grace" (3:24)
Say what propitiation means in 3:25 in the passage's context

nodes.d: Paul uses Abraham to show that righteousness is counted to the one who believes, before circumcision, and that Abraham is the father of all who believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Romans 4 uses Genesis 15:6?
ev: Link Romans 4:3 to Genesis 15:6
Explain why it matters that Abraham was counted righteous before circumcision (4:9-12)

nodes.d: Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ; Christ died for us while we were sinners.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 5:8 says about God's love?
ev: State what believers have according to 5:1-2
Explain 5:8

nodes.d: As sin and death came into the world through one man, so grace and righteousness come through one man, Jesus Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast between Adam and Christ in Romans 5?
ev: Compare Adam and Christ in 5:15-19
Connect 5:12 to Genesis 3

nodes.t: Dead to sin, alive to God
nodes.d: Believers are united with Christ in his death and resurrection and are to consider themselves dead to sin and alive to God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what it means to be dead to sin and alive to God (6:11)?
ev: Explain what baptism pictures in 6:3-4
State 6:11

nodes.d: Believers, freed from sin, become servants of righteousness; the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 6:23?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 6:23

nodes.d: Paul explains the law's relationship to sin and describes the struggle with sin in the one who delights in God's law.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Paul says the law is good for and what it cannot do (Romans 7)?
ev: Explain 7:12
Describe the struggle in 7:15-25

nodes.t: No condemnation: life in the Spirit
nodes.d: There is now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus; those led by the Spirit of God are sons of God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 8:1 and what it means to be a son of God (8:14-15)?
ev: State 8:1
Explain adoption in 8:14-17

nodes.d: Believers receive the Spirit of adoption and cry "Abba, Father", being heirs with Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 8:15-17 says about being God's children?
ev: Explain "Spirit of adoption" (8:15)

nodes.d: God works all things for good to those who love him, and those he foreknew he predestined, called, justified and glorified.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the steps of Romans 8:29-30?
ev: List the steps in 8:29-30 in order

nodes.t: Nothing can separate us from the love of God
nodes.d: Paul concludes that nothing in creation can separate believers from the love of God in Christ Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the end of Romans 8?
ev: Read 8:38-39 and list what Paul says cannot separate us

nodes.d: Paul answers the question of Israel by pointing to God's sovereign choice, from Isaac and Jacob onward, and his mercy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 9 says about God's choice and mercy?
ev: Link 9:7 to Genesis 21:12 and 9:12 to Genesis 25:23
Explain 9:15-16

nodes.d: Righteousness is for everyone who believes; faith comes by hearing the word of Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 10:9-10 and 10:17?
ev: State 10:9-10
Explain 10:17

nodes.t: The remnant and the olive tree
nodes.d: God has not cast off his people; a remnant is saved by grace, and Gentiles are grafted into the olive tree.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the olive tree picture in Romans 11?
ev: Explain the olive tree illustration in 11:17-24
Say how the chapter ends (11:33-36)

nodes.d: In view of God's mercies, believers present their bodies as a living sacrifice, are transformed by the renewing of the mind, and live in love as members of one body.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Romans 12:1-2?
ev: Explain 12:1-2
List ways Paul describes love in practice (12:9-21)

nodes.d: Paul teaches submission to governing authorities as God's servants, and sums up the law in love for neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Romans 13:1-7 teaches?
ev: State what Paul says about authorities (13:1-7)
Explain 13:8-10

nodes.d: Believers are to welcome one another, not judge over disputable matters, and seek the good of their neighbour.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says to treat a brother who disagrees on disputable matters?
ev: Explain 14:1 and 14:17

nodes.d: Paul's plans, personal greetings, a warning, and the closing benediction and doxology.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say how Romans ends?
ev: Read the doxology (16:25-27)

nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.d: The serpent tempts the woman; she and the man eat the fruit God forbade and hide from God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how sin entered the world in Genesis 3?
ev: Retell the temptation and the disobedience in order
Explain what the man and woman did when God called

nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.t: Abram believed and it was counted as righteousness
nodes.d: Genesis 15:6 records that Abram believed the LORD and it was counted to him as righteousness, the verse Paul explains in Romans 4.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Genesis 15:6 in their own words?
ev: Quote or paraphrase 15:6 accurately
Say who or what Abram believed

nodes.d: God appears to Abram at ninety-nine, changes his name to Abraham, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what circumcision was a sign of in Genesis 17?
ev: Explain the name change (17:5)
State what circumcision signified (17:10-11)

nodes.d: God keeps his promise: Sarah bears Isaac to Abraham in his old age.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Isaac was born?
ev: Retell how God kept his promise

nodes.d: Esau sells his birthright to Jacob, and Jacob later receives Isaac's blessing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jacob received the birthright and the blessing?
ev: Retell the birthright and blessing episodes
Note God's word to Rebekah in 25:23

nodes.t: God meant it for good: providence
nodes.d: Joseph tells his brothers that although they meant evil, God meant it for good (50:20); Paul teaches a similar confidence in Romans 8:28.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joseph meant in Genesis 50:20?
ev: Explain Genesis 50:20 in context
Compare it with Romans 8:28

nodes.t: The LORD visits Abraham and Sarah
nodes.d: The LORD appears to Abraham in the plains of Mamre as three men; Abraham hurries to feed them. One says Sarah will have a son at the appointed time, Sarah laughs inside the tent, and the LORD asks whether anything is too hard for Him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the visitors promised Sarah and why she laughed?
ev: Describe Abraham's hospitality to the three men (18:2-8)
Repeat the question the LORD asks in 18:14 and say what it is about

nodes.t: Hagar and Ishmael are sent away
nodes.d: After Isaac is weaned, Sarah sees Ishmael mocking and asks that he and Hagar be cast out. God tells Abraham that his seed will be called in Isaac but he will also make a nation of Ishmael; in the wilderness God hears the boy's voice and opens Hagar's eyes to a well.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised about Ishmael, even as Isaac was the child of promise?
ev: Say what God told Abraham in 21:12-13
Describe how God provided for Hagar and Ishmael in the wilderness (21:17-20)

nodes.d: God tells Pharaoh he has raised him up to show his power and make his name known in all the earth, and sends hail with fire that destroys everything in the fields, except in Goshen. Pharaoh says he has sinned and the LORD is righteous, but hardens his heart again when the hail stops.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Pharaoh said after the hail and what he did once it stopped?
ev: Say why God said he had raised Pharaoh up (9:16)
Say what some servants did when they feared the word of the LORD (9:20)
Describe Pharaoh's confession and what followed (9:27-35)

nodes.t: Moses asks to see God's glory
nodes.d: Moses asks that God's presence go with them and then to see his glory. The LORD says his presence will go with Moses, that he will make all his goodness pass and proclaim his name, but no man can see his face and live; Moses is hidden in a cleft of the rock and sees only his back.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Moses asked to see and how God answered?
ev: Say what Moses asked in 33:15 and 33:18
Say what God said he would do and what he would not allow (33:19-23)

nodes.d: Leviticus gives the LORD's instructions from the tabernacle: the offerings, the consecration of the priests, clean and unclean, the day of atonement, holy living, the feasts, the jubilee, and the blessings and curses of obedience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a one-sentence summary of what Leviticus is about?
ev: Name the main sections of Leviticus (offerings, priests, clean and unclean, atonement, holiness, feasts, jubilee, blessings and curses).

nodes.t: Not like Egypt or Canaan: sexual boundaries
nodes.d: Leviticus 18 calls Israel not to follow the practices of Egypt or Canaan, listing forbidden sexual relations, Molech worship and other practices, and warns that the land vomits out nations that defile it.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the chapter says the LORD is giving these commands, using what verses 3 and 24-30 say?
ev: Say whose ways Israel is told not to follow (18:3).
State the consequence the chapter gives for defiling the land (18:24-28).
Find 18:5 and say what it promises to the person who does the LORD's statutes.

nodes.t: "Ye shall be holy": laws for neighbours
nodes.d: Leviticus 19 gathers commands under the call to be holy because the LORD is holy: honouring parents, sabbaths, leaving gleanings for the poor, honest dealing, no partiality, loving one's neighbour as oneself, care for the stranger and just weights.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some ways Leviticus 19 says holiness shows up in daily life?
ev: Name at least five commands from the chapter that deal with how to treat other people.
Find the command to love the neighbour (19:18) and the command about the stranger (19:33-34).

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 5 has Moses remind Israel that the LORD made a covenant with them at Horeb, repeats the ten commandments given from the fire, and recounts the people's fear and Moses standing between them and the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list the ten commandments and explain who gave them and to whom?
ev: Say the ten commandments in order.
Say what 5:2-3 says about whom the covenant was made with.
Find the reason attached to the sabbath commandment here (5:15).

nodes.t: Return to the LORD; the word is near; choose life
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 30 says that when blessing and curse have come and Israel returns and obeys, the LORD will gather them, bring them to the land, and circumcise their hearts; the commandment is not hidden or far off but very near, and Moses sets life and death before them and calls them to choose life.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the choice set before Israel in Deuteronomy 30:15-20?
ev: Say what the LORD promises when Israel returns (30:1-6).
Say what 30:11-14 says about where the word is.
Say the choice in 30:19.

nodes.d: Deuteronomy 32:1-43 is a song that praises the LORD as the Rock whose work is perfect, recalls his care for Jacob in the wilderness, accuses Israel of forgetting him and worshipping other gods, tells of judgment, yet says vengeance is the LORD's and he will judge his people and be merciful to his land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarize the song in three parts: the LORD's faithfulness, Israel's unfaithfulness and the LORD's judgment and mercy?
ev: Describe the picture of the LORD as the Rock in 32:3-4.
Summarize what Israel did in return for his care (32:15-18).

nodes.d: 1 Kings opens with David old and Solomon made king (1:1-53), moves through Solomon's wisdom, temple and decline, then the division of the kingdom and the prophets Elijah and Micaiah under Israel's kings, ending with Ahab's death and Jehoshaphat and Ahaziah (22:53).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline 1 Kings in order, from Solomon's accession to Ahab's death?
ev: Name the main phases: Solomon's accession, the temple, the divided kingdom, Elijah and Ahab
Say how the book begins (David's old age) and ends (Ahaziah of Israel)

nodes.t: The LORD speaks to Elijah at Horeb
nodes.d: At Horeb Elijah complains that he alone is left; the LORD is not in the wind, earthquake or fire but in a still small voice, and sends him to anoint Hazael, Jehu and Elisha, saying he has left seven thousand who have not bowed to Baal.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD told Elijah at Horeb and how he spoke?
ev: Describe the wind, earthquake, fire and voice
State the three people Elijah was told to anoint and the number left in Israel

nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalms 5-7: prayers for help against enemies and for the LORD’s judgment
nodes.d: Psalm 5 is a morning prayer to a God who hates wickedness, Psalm 6 is a weary cry for mercy and healing, and Psalm 7 appeals to the LORD as righteous judge to save the speaker from persecutors.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how each of Psalms 5, 6 and 7 begins and what the speaker asks?
ev: Find the request in 5:8, the groaning in 6:6, and the appeal to God’s judgment in 7:8-9.

nodes.t: Psalms 9-10: the LORD is a refuge for the oppressed and judges the wicked
nodes.d: Psalm 9 praises the LORD who sits on his throne judging, is a refuge for the oppressed and does not forget the cry of the humble; Psalm 10 asks why he stands afar and describes the wicked who persecute the poor, ending with the LORD hearing the humble.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalms 9 and 10 speak of the LORD as judge of the oppressor?
ev: List what the wicked say and do in Psalm 10:2-11, and the LORD’s response in 10:16-18.

nodes.t: Psalms 14 and 53: the fool says there is no God
nodes.d: Both psalms say the fool has said in his heart there is no God, that the LORD looked down from heaven to see if any seek him, and that all are gone aside and none does good; the psalms end with a longing for the salvation of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} compare Psalms 14 and 53 and say what they teach about human beings?
ev: Compare Psalm 14:1-3 and 53:1-3 and note the repeated words.
Find the closing wish in 14:7 and 53:6.

nodes.t: Psalm 18: the LORD my rock and deliverer; a king’s thanksgiving
nodes.d: The speaker loves the LORD as rock, fortress and deliverer, describes God coming down in storm and fire to rescue him from death and strong enemies, and gives thanks for strength in battle and for deliverance given to his king and anointed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Psalm 18 pictures the LORD rescuing the speaker?
ev: Read 18:1-6, 18:30-36 and 18:50 and list who delivers and who is delivered.

nodes.t: Psalm 19: the heavens declare God’s glory, and his law is perfect
nodes.d: The heavens declare the glory of God day and night to all the earth, and the law, testimony, statutes and judgments of the LORD are perfect, sure, right and sweeter than honey; the speaker asks to be cleansed from secret and presumptuous sins.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how God makes himself known in Psalm 19 through the heavens and through his law?
ev: Read 19:1-6 and 19:7-11 and say what each half says about God.
Read 19:12-14 as a prayer.

nodes.t: Psalm 32: blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven
nodes.d: The speaker says the one whose transgression is forgiven is blessed, describes bones wasting while he kept silent about his sin, and says that when he acknowledged his sin to the LORD he was forgiven and now the LORD is his hiding place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happens in Psalm 32:5 when the speaker confesses his sin?
ev: Contrast 32:3-4 with 32:5.
Read 32:1-2 and note who is called blessed.

nodes.t: Psalm 36: the wicked and the fountain of life
nodes.d: The transgression of the wicked says there is no fear of God before his eyes, while the LORD’s mercy reaches to the heavens and his faithfulness to the clouds; with him is the fountain of life and in his light we see light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} contrast what Psalm 36 says about the wicked and about the LORD?
ev: Contrast 36:1-4 with 36:5-9.

nodes.t: Psalm 44: a lament of God’s people after defeat
nodes.d: The people recall what God did for their fathers in giving the land, say they trust not in their bow, but now God has cast them off, scattered them and made them a reproach though they have not forgotten him, and they ask him to awake and redeem them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the people complain in Psalm 44 and what they ask?
ev: Read 44:1-8, 44:9-16 and 44:17-26 and say what each section says.

nodes.t: Psalm 69: zeal for thy house; they gave me vinegar
nodes.d: The speaker is sinking in deep waters and hated without cause, says zeal for God’s house has consumed him and reproaches have fallen on him, that he was given gall and vinegar, asks that his adversaries’ table be a snare and their eyes darkened, and ends with praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the suffering in Psalm 69:1-4 and 69:20-21 and how the psalm ends?
ev: Read 69:1-4, 69:9, 69:21 and 69:22-28 and list what the speaker suffers and asks.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.t: Psalms 140-142: deliver me from violent men; I cried unto the LORD
nodes.d: Psalm 140 asks the LORD to deliver the speaker from evil and violent men whose tongues are like serpents; Psalm 141 asks that his prayer be set before the LORD like incense and that he be kept from wickedness; Psalm 142 pours out his complaint, saying the LORD is his refuge and portion.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 141:2-4 and 142:5 say about the speaker’s prayer and refuge?
ev: Read 140:1-3, 141:1-4 and 142:1-7 and list what the speaker asks.

nodes.d: Proverbs begins with the proverbs of Solomon son of David (1:1), sets out a father’s teaching about wisdom and folly (1-9), gathers many short sayings (10-29), and ends with the words of Agur (30) and of king Lemuel (31).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name the main sections of Proverbs and who is named as the source of each?
ev: Describe the main sections of Proverbs: 1-9, 10-22, 22-24, 25-29, 30, 31.

nodes.t: More proverbs of Solomon: kings, neighbours and fitting words (25)
nodes.d: These proverbs, which the men of Hezekiah king of Judah copied out, speak of the glory of God to conceal a thing and the honour of kings to search it out, a word fitly spoken, restraint with a neighbour, and kindness to an enemy.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 25:1 says about the source of chapters 25-29 and give one saying from chapter 25?
ev: Read 25:1 and say who copied these proverbs.
Find the saying about a word fitly spoken (25:11).

nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: The Lord charges his rebellious children
nodes.d: The LORD calls heaven and earth to witness that the children he raised have rebelled, rejects their empty sacrifices, and offers cleansing if they are willing and obedient.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says he is weary of sacrifices in Isaiah 1 and what he commands instead?
ev: Retell the charge of Isaiah 1:2-4
Explain why God rejects the sacrifices in 1:11-15 and what he asks instead in 1:16-17
Quote the offer in 1:18-20

nodes.d: Isaiah writes a name-sign for a son, the LORD warns that the king of Assyria will flood Judah, tells Isaiah not to fear what the people fear, and calls him to the law and testimony instead of mediums.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD says to sanctify him rather than fear what the people fear in Isaiah 8:11-13?
ev: Explain the meaning of the child's name sign in 8:1-4
Say whom Isaiah is told to fear and sanctify (8:12-13)
Explain the contrast between the law and testimony and consulting the dead (8:19-20)

nodes.d: The LORD sends Assyria as the rod of his anger against a hypocritical nation, but punishes the king of Assyria for his boasting; a remnant will return and Zion is told not to fear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the picture of the axe boasting against the one who swings it in Isaiah 10:15?
ev: Explain how Assyria is both used and judged (10:5-7, 12-15)
Say what is promised to the remnant (10:20-23)
Describe the comfort given to Zion in 10:24-27

nodes.t: The shoot from the stem of Jesse
nodes.d: A shoot from Jesse's stem, endowed with the Spirit of the LORD, judges the poor with righteousness; peace reaches even the animals, the earth is full of the knowledge of the LORD, and the remnant is gathered.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the one who comes from the stem of Jesse and the peace of his kingdom in Isaiah 11?
ev: List the gifts of the Spirit resting on him in Isaiah 11:2
Describe how he judges (11:3-5)
Describe the peaceful creation in 11:6-9 and the gathering in 11:10-12

nodes.t: Woe to Ephraim's drunkards and the scoffers in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Isaiah rebukes the drunken leaders, who mock his teaching, boast of a covenant with death, and are promised a tested cornerstone laid in Zion; the farmer's patient work illustrates God's wise ways.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the scoffers in Isaiah 28:15 relied on and what the LORD lays in Zion in 28:16?
ev: Describe the scoffers' covenant with death (28:15)
Quote what the LORD lays in Zion (28:16)
Explain the farmer illustration in 28:23-29

nodes.t: Woe to Ariel: a sealed vision and a marvellous work
nodes.d: The LORD besieges Ariel, the city where David dwelt, then saves it from the nations; the people honour him with lips but not hearts, the vision is like a sealed book, and the deaf will hear and the blind see.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 29:13 says about the people's worship?
ev: Describe the siege and sudden deliverance of Ariel (29:1-8)
Explain the charge in 29:13
Describe the change promised in 29:17-24

nodes.t: Comfort my people: the incomparable God
nodes.d: God tells his prophets to comfort Jerusalem because her iniquity is pardoned, a voice prepares the way of the LORD, the LORD comes as shepherd, and no one compares to him who gives strength to the weary.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the LORD comforts Jerusalem in Isaiah 40:1-2 and who the LORD is compared to in 40:12-26?
ev: Quote the command and reason in Isaiah 40:1-2
Describe the voice crying in the wilderness (40:3-5)
Explain what 40:28-31 says about those who wait on the LORD

nodes.t: Cyrus, the LORD's shepherd and anointed
nodes.d: The LORD names Cyrus, by name before his time, as his shepherd and anointed who will let Jerusalem and the temple be rebuilt, so that all will know there is none else.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says Cyrus will do and why in Isaiah 44:28-45:6?
ev: Say what the LORD says of Cyrus (44:28, 45:1)
Explain why the LORD calls Cyrus by name (45:4-6)
Quote the invitation in 45:22-23

nodes.t: Awake, Zion: good tidings of peace
nodes.d: Jerusalem is told to put on strength, she is redeemed without money, the feet of the one who brings good tidings are beautiful, and the LORD has bared his arm before the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 52:7 describes about the one who brings good tidings?
ev: Quote 52:7
Say what the watchmen see (52:8)
Describe the command to depart in 52:11-12

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Your iniquities have separated; the Redeemer comes
nodes.d: The LORD's hand is not short, but iniquities separate the people from God; he sees no intercessor, so his own arm brings salvation, and the Redeemer comes to Zion with a covenant that his Spirit and words will not depart.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what has separated the people from God in Isaiah 59:1-2 and how the LORD responds?
ev: Quote Isaiah 59:1-2
List sins in 59:3-8
Say what the LORD does when he sees no intercessor (59:16-17) and the covenant of 59:21

nodes.t: New heavens and a new earth
nodes.d: The LORD answers a rebellious people, saves a remnant of his servants, and creates new heavens and a new earth and Jerusalem a joy where weeping is no more and the wolf and lamb feed together.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the LORD says he will create in Isaiah 65:17-25?
ev: Say who the LORD preserves and who he judges (65:8-15)
Describe the new heavens and new earth (65:17-25)

nodes.d: Hosea's word to Israel in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash and Judah's kings: a prophet's marriage to an unfaithful wife pictures the LORD's love for faithless Israel, followed by charges, judgment and a call to return.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences how Hosea's marriage pictures the LORD's relationship with Israel?
ev: Say that Hosea's marriage (chs 1-3) is an acted picture of the LORD and Israel
Outline the book as marriage (1-3), charges and judgment (4-13) and a closing call to return (14)

nodes.d: The LORD tells Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms; their three children are named Jezreel, Loruhamah and Loammi as signs, yet the chapter ends with a promise that Israel will be called sons of the living God.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the names of Hosea's three children meant and what hope the LORD adds at the end of chapter 1?
ev: Name the three children and what each name signals
Point out the promise in 1:10-11 that reverses 'not my people'

nodes.t: The LORD pleads and allures his wife
nodes.d: The LORD charges Israel with going after her lovers and forgetting him, announces discipline, then promises to allure her into the wilderness and betroth her to himself for ever in faithfulness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how chapter 2 moves from judgment on Israel to the LORD betrothing her again?
ev: Describe the charge (2:5, 2:8, 2:13) and the discipline (2:6-13)
Describe the promise to betroth Israel for ever (2:19-20) and to say 'Thou art my people' (2:23)

nodes.d: The word of the LORD to Joel: a locust plague and the near day of the LORD, a call to return with all the heart, the LORD's promise of restoration and of his Spirit poured out, and judgment on the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of Joel and say where the 'day of the LORD' appears?
ev: Outline the book: plague (1), call and promise (2), nations judged (3)
Say what the phrase 'day of the LORD' is used for in 1:15 and 2:1

nodes.t: Restoration and the Spirit poured out
nodes.d: The LORD pities his people, drives off the northern army, restores the years the locust has eaten, and promises afterward to pour out his Spirit on all flesh, with wonders before the day of the LORD and deliverance for all who call on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promise of 2:28-29 and the promise to whoever calls on the name of the LORD?
ev: List the restoration promises of 2:19-27
Say who receives the Spirit in 2:28-29
Read the promise of 2:32

nodes.d: The burden Habakkuk saw: his complaints about violence in Judah and the LORD's answers, the vision to wait for in which the just live by faith, woes on the proud, and a prayer ending in rejoicing in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Habakkuk moves from complaint to rejoicing?
ev: Describe the pattern of complaint and answer in chapters 1-2
Say how the book ends (3:17-19)

nodes.t: The vision to wait for; the just live by faith
nodes.d: Habakkuk stands on his watch; the LORD tells him to write the vision, which will surely come though it tarries, and contrasts the proud, whose soul is not upright, with the just, who shall live by his faith.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the contrast of Habakkuk 2:4 and say what the LORD tells Habakkuk to do with the vision?
ev: Say what Habakkuk does and what the LORD tells him to do (2:1-3)
Read 2:4 and state the contrast
Find where Paul cites it (Romans 1:17)

nodes.d: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi: a series of disputes in which the LORD states a charge, the people ask how, and he answers, ending with the coming day of the LORD and the promise to send Elijah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how Malachi's disputes work and how the book ends?
ev: Notice the pattern of 'Wherein?' questions (1:2, 1:6, 2:17, 3:7-8)
Say how the book ends (4:5-6)

nodes.d: The LORD says he loved Israel, and when they ask how, he points to Jacob and Esau, saying he loved Jacob and hated Esau and laid waste Esau's mountains; he promises that he will be magnified from the border of Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the LORD answers the question 'Wherein hast thou loved us?' in Malachi 1:2-3?
ev: Read the exchange of 1:2
Say what happens to Edom's plans (1:4)

nodes.d: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?
ev: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3
